reasoning: Plan A is significantly better for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates targeted training elements crucial for improving speed and trail performance. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost entirely on recovery and easy runs, which while important for overall health, won't actively develop the physiological adaptations required for faster times. Plan A’s structured approach, with its blend of aerobic endurance, hill work, and a longer run, provides a more effective pathway to improved trail running speed.
